hero.heading: Burnside Express Collision, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built October 4, 2026, from burnside-express.com, the shops' listings, the press, the industry's billing survey, and federal data. Every number is labeled: published, federal, or our assumption. The assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: (exact: $3,811 and $34,592) Under $5,000 a figure rounds to the nearest $1,000, above it to the nearest $5,000; the exact figures govern.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Repairs across your shops in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per hundred repairs.

sliders.label: Share of repairs at the two shops that are not your best
Extra cost of one repair against your best shop
sliders.basis: In supplements, days, and rework. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Not-included operations performed and never billed, per repair
Months between estimate and parts order
sliders.basis: Half a month to two months, about two to eight weeks. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

constants.text: Federal series: BLS producer price index, motor vehicle parts (WPU1412), 145.456 in October 2025 to 149.359 in August 2026, its latest published month: up 2.7 percent over ten months, 0.27 percent per month [[BENCHMARK]]. The model applies it only across the weeks between estimate and parts order. Next release October 15, 2026; this page changes with it.

terms.label: Parts drift between estimate and order

model.formulaText: Moved per 100 repairs = 100 × share at the other two shops × extra cost per repair + 100 × unbilled operations per repair × value per operation + 100 × parts per repair × months of lag × (149.359 ÷ 145.456 minus 1) ÷ 10
model.plainText: In words, what a repair costs at your other two shops beyond what the same repair costs at your best one, plus the not-included operations performed and never written, plus what parts prices add while an estimate waits for its parts order.
model.callout: What nobody counts across three shops is the gap between the best one and the other two. Same name, same guarantee, three estimators, three ways of writing a supplement and three cycle times; the industry's own survey of 473 shops says the not-included operations one estimator writes every time, another never writes at all, and that one shop in five never asks. The best of your three already runs the way you want the fourth to run; nobody has written down what it does differently.

smallRound.note: Under $5,000, a figure rounds to the nearest $1,000.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: Twenty years as a technician and then your own door in 2016, for a reason you put on record: to treat employees better [[BENCHMARK]].
Three shops now, West Indianapolis, Zionsville, and Greenwood, every one I-CAR Gold Class, with calibration done in-house and a lifetime guarantee on the work [[OBSERVED]].
More than two thousand customers rating you on whether you kept them informed and finished on time [[OBSERVED]].
A plan you have said aloud, to open more doors across Indiana, in a trade where most independents are selling theirs [[BENCHMARK]].

proposal.heading: What we propose
proposal.lead: The proposal: the count by shop (supplements, days, rework, lines written and paid), the best shop's page written in its people's words as the standard for the other two and the fourth, and the thirty-day result; fixed fee between $1,500 and $2,500; read-only; no customer or vehicle identity leaves the buildings.

ledger.title: What a quarter of the count by shop looks like
ledger.label: Illustrative, not Burnside Express Collision data

rows.flag: The standard the other two are measured against.

ledger.note: Illustrative costs. The count prices the real gap from the company's own records. Here the gap against the best shop uses $90 for each extra supplement and $43 for each not-included line left unwritten; cycle days and ready on time are shown, not priced. Every shop and figure is invented to show the format.

proposal.promise: If your records show our printed range overstated your exposure, our findings letter says so in those words.
